title: Agreement of runs before an anchor visit
statement: Let $M$ and $N$ be deterministic machines with $k$ work tapes over the Boolean alphabet and state set $S$, and designate a state $q_a$. Suppose their transitions agree in every state other than $q_a$, for every input symbol and every tuple of work-tape readings. For any configuration $c$ on input $x$ and any $t\in\mathbb N$, if the run of $N$ from $c$ is never in state $q_a$ at any time $j<t$, then the two machines' configurations after $t$ steps from $c$ are equal.
hypotheses_covered: A natural number of work tapes and state set $S$
Two machines $M,N$ over the Boolean alphabet
Their transition functions agree at every state other than $q_a$, for all readings
At every time $j<t$, the run of $N$ from $c$ is not in state $q_a$
replaced:
If two transition tables agree at every control state other than a designated
anchor state, then their runs from a common configuration coincide for every
duration during which the second machine's run has not yet visited the anchor.
